exposure: Intravenous magnesium sulphate (50 mg/kg bolus dose in 100 ml normal saline)
outcome: Total analgesic requirement in the first 24 hours postoperative period
Incidence of complications (sedation, hypotension, shivering, nausea, vomiting, pruritus)
cohort: 50 patients aged 20-65 years, ASA Grade I & II, undergoing lower limb orthopaedic surgery with spinal anaesthesia.
finding: Intravenous magnesium sulphate significantly prolonged the time to rescue analgesia and reduced the total analgesic requirement in the first 24 hours post-surgery for lower limb orthopaedic patients, without significantly increasing complications.
